question: The number of elements known at the time of Russian chemist Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev was:
solution:
The correct answer is __**63.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The number of elements known at the time of **Mendeleev **was **63.**
 
• This is because Mendeleev's periodic table included **63 elements,** arranged in order of increasing **atomic mass.**
 
• Some of the elements he predicted, such as **gallium and germanium,** were discovered later and found to fit into the gaps he had left in the table.
 
• Today, we know of **118 elements** in total, with the most recent additions being **nihonium, moscovium, tennessine, and oganesson**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev** is known for creating the **first periodic table** of elements.
 
• He arranged the elements based on their **atomic mass** and observed that there was a **periodicity** in their properties.
 
• **Mendeleev **predicted the existence of some elements that were yet to be discovered, and left gaps in his periodic table for them.
 
• **57** is the number of elements known at the time of Swedish chemist **Jundefinedns Jacob Berzelius**, who is known for discovering several new elements and developing the modern system of chemical symbols.
 
• **53** is the number of elements known at the time of English chemist** John Dalton**, who is known for developing the atomic theory of matter.
 
• **67** is the number of elements known at the time of American chemist **Glenn T. Seaborg, **who discovered several new elements and contributed to the development of the actinide series of elements.
